# DroidHand tools

<!-- Generated by mcp-server/scripts/gen-tools-doc.ts (npm run docs:tools). Do not edit by hand. -->

37 MCP tools in 9 areas. Tools are forwarded to the phone unless marked **local (host)**, in which case the relay daemon handles them itself.

Notes column: the risk **tier** recorded in the audit log; **confirm on device** means the app asks the user to approve the action on the phone first.

## Shared arguments

- `display`: display id (0 = phone screen; bg_open id = background). On 0, if the user is using the phone the app may ask them first: errors 'awaiting_user' (retry shortly) or 'user_declined' (use bg_open instead).
- `device`: phone id (see list_devices); may be left out when only one phone is connected.
- `ref`: stable element ref from screen_snapshot, e.g. '@4'.
- `split`: experimental, with move=true display=0 and the shell helper: put the moved app in split screen next to the user's app.
- `reason`: why adb is needed, shown in the audit log.

Every tool that is not local also accepts `display`, and every tool that acts on one phone accepts `device`; both are left out of the tables below.

## Perception

Read what is on screen and on the device.

| Tool | What it does | Inputs | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `screen_snapshot` | Accessibility tree of the foreground window: up to 300 visible nodes, each with a @ref (for tap/type_text), role, text or description, resource id, center x,y and clickable/editable/checked/scrollable flags. Passwords are masked. | — | standard |
| `screen_capture` | JPEG screenshot of the current screen (base64), at most 720 px wide. Secure screens (e.g. the PIN pad) come out black. | `quality` number 1–100 (optional) | standard |
| `get_foreground_app` | Package name of the app in the foreground. | — | standard |
| `list_windows` | Windows on screen as the accessibility service sees them (type, layer, active/focused, package). | — | standard |
| `list_apps` | Launchable apps (package and label), sorted by label. | — | standard |

## Interaction

Touch, type and press keys through the accessibility service.

| Tool | What it does | Inputs | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tap` | Tap an element by ref, or raw x,y. | `ref` string (optional)<br>`x` number (optional)<br>`y` number (optional) | standard |
| `long_press` | Long-press an element or point. | `ref` string (optional)<br>`x` number (optional)<br>`y` number (optional)<br>`durationMs` number (optional) | standard |
| `swipe` | Swipe from one point to another. | `fromX` number<br>`fromY` number<br>`toX` number<br>`toY` number<br>`durationMs` number (optional) | standard |
| `scroll` | Scroll the screen in a direction (a swipe across its middle; 'down' reveals what is below). | `direction` "up" \| "down" \| "left" \| "right" | standard |
| `type_text` | Type text into the focused field (or a ref), optionally pressing enter. | `text` string<br>`ref` string (optional)<br>`submit` boolean (optional) | standard |
| `key_event` | Press a navigation key. On an own-window background display only back, enter and (Android 14+) home; recents is refused there because it opens on the user's main screen. | `key` "back" \| "home" \| "recents" \| "notifications" \| "quick_settings" \| "enter" | standard |
| `global_action` | Perform a global accessibility action on the main screen (refused with display=&lt;background id&gt;). split_screen toggles split screen with the app on top of the main screen (e.g. after launch_app move=true display=0, so the user continues it next to their own app). | `action` "notifications" \| "quick_settings" \| "screenshot" \| "lock_screen" \| "split_screen" | standard |

## Apps & navigation

Launch apps, open links and go home.

| Tool | What it does | Inputs | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `launch_app` | Launch an app by package name (display=&lt;id&gt; for a background display; bounds=[l,t,r,b] px opens a One UI pop-up window on the main screen). On a background display it opens a separate copy, so the user's own copy stays on their screen. move=true reuses the app's existing task instead and moves it: with display=&lt;id&gt; it takes the user's copy to the background display (only when the user asked: it leaves their screen); with display=0 it brings the copy from the background display to the main screen ('continue on the main screen', e.g. for the user to take over). With the shell helper running (own_helper_start) the exact task from the background display is moved and bounds turn it into a pop-up window; without it Android may pick the user's own copy if the app is also open on the main screen, and bounds are ignored. The background display has the phone screen's size by default, so a moved app keeps its state instead of being recreated. What works differs per phone: see docs/devices.md. | `package` string<br>`bounds` number[4] (optional)<br>`move` boolean (optional)<br>`split` boolean (optional) | standard |
| `open_url` | Open a URL in the default app for it. With display=&lt;id&gt; it opens on that background display, in the agent's own copy of the browser (the user's browser on the main screen is left alone). | `url` string (URL) | standard |
| `go_home` | Go to the home screen (on a background display: the home key; not available on Android 13 and older). | — | standard |

## Lock screen

Lock state and opt-in PIN unlock (the PIN never leaves the phone).

| Tool | What it does | Inputs | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `get_lock_state` | Screen on/off, locked, secure lock, and whether PIN unlock by the agent is enabled. | — | standard |
| `unlock_device` | Unlock the phone with the PIN the user saved in the DroidHand app (opt-in, off by default; the PIN never leaves the phone). Wakes the screen, opens the PIN pad and enters it. One wrong attempt disables the feature. Only when the task needs the main screen. | — | privileged |

## ADB on demand

Debugging stays off; short, time-limited ADB sessions for privileged work.

| Tool | What it does | Inputs | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `adb_session_begin` | Turn USB debugging on and connect this computer to the phone over the tailnet (works on mobile data). Debugging is OFF the rest of the time: open a session only when a task really needs adb (e.g. `pm grant`, `pm install`, `dumpsys`) and ALWAYS call adb_session_end as soon as you are done. Fallback only: the session closes by itself 10 minutes after your last tool call (each call renews it), so a lost connection never leaves debugging on. The phone shows a 'Turn ADB off' notification meanwhile. The first session after a reboot needs the phone on any Wi-Fi (error 'adb_not_armed' otherwise). Test phones set to adb mode "always" (see list_devices) only connect: their debugging is never turned off. | `reason` string | privileged · local (host) |
| `adb_shell` | Run a shell command (as the adb shell user) in the open ADB session. Returns stdout, stderr and exitCode. Commands that would leave the agent no way back to the phone (stopping, disabling or removing DroidHand or Tailscale, turning debugging, accessibility or the network off, rebooting) are refused with lockout_guard: use adb_session_end to turn debugging off. | `command` string<br>`timeoutSeconds` number 1–300 (optional) | privileged · local (host) |
| `adb_session_end` | Close the ADB session and turn debugging off on the phone right away (also stops the own-window helper). Call it as soon as the adb work is done. | — | standard · local (host) |

## Background display

Work on a separate display while the user keeps using the phone.

| Tool | What it does | Inputs | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bg_open` | Open a background display and return its displayId; then pass display=&lt;id&gt; to launch_app, screen_snapshot, screen_capture, tap, swipe, scroll, type_text, key_event. mode: 'native' (system window, works with debugging OFF, cannot be hidden), 'own' (our window: hideable, resizable, user can interact; needs own_helper_start, i.e. an ADB session), 'auto' (default: the own window whenever ADB can be turned on — the relay opens an ADB session just for it and turns debugging off at bg_close — else native. Prefer it: the own window never takes the focus from the user's screen, so their keyboard stays; on the native window any touch or new screen closes it, so use refs there). The user's choice in the app overrides mode (see forcedByUser). Safety: work in the background only happens while the user can see it (stop button + window, eye bubble or handle). If those cannot be shown, the session is closed and calls fail with 'indicators_not_visible' — do not retry in a loop. width/height/dpi default to the phone screen's, so apps can move between the screens (launch_app move=true) without being recreated. | `mode` "auto" \| "native" \| "own" (optional)<br>`width` number (optional)<br>`height` number (optional)<br>`dpi` number (optional) | standard |
| `bg_status` | Background display state: mode, displayId, hidden, helpPending, user's method choice, own helper availability. | — | standard |
| `bg_hide` | Hide the own-window background display (the agent keeps working; the user sees an eye bubble). | — | standard |
| `bg_show` | Show the background window again. | — | standard |
| `bg_close` | Close the background display (own: its apps are closed; native: Android moves them to the main screen, on Samsung on top of the user's app — move or close them first). | — | standard |
| `request_user_help` | Ask the user to take over in the background window (e.g. captcha, login). Shows the window with the message; poll bg_status until helpPending is null (the user taps the message when done). | `message` string | standard |
| `own_helper_start` | Start the shell helper over ADB (opens an ADB session if none is open; see adb_session_begin). Enables the 'own' background-window method. The helper dies when the ADB session ends (debugging off): call adb_session_end when the background task is done. | — | privileged · local (host) |
| `own_helper_stop` | Stop the shell helper (closes own-window background displays). | — | standard · local (host) |

## Safety

Audit trail and kill switch.

| Tool | What it does | Inputs | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `get_audit_log` | Return the path to the append-only audit log. | — | standard · local (host) |
| `panic_disconnect` | Stop at once: cancel the running action, close the background window, end the ADB session (debugging off, except on adb mode 'always') and drop the phone's connection; the phone reconnects by itself a few seconds later. It never switches the app off (only the user can, on the phone). Without device: every phone. | — | standard · local (host) |
